brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Built a 3-cell row of full hex bases (piece:-1,0,0; piece:0,0,0; piece:1,0,0) with three two-compartment full-depth bins (bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0) as open cubby shelves, joined with joint bolts. Bins are the shelving; no separate shelf boards were added.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only and has no load rating. Nothing in the build proves 50 kg; the printed plastic material and joints are not verified for load. Not claimed.
Two drawers: drawer:0#0,-1#cut and drawer:0#1,-1#cut, on the cut faces of the half bases piece:0,-1,0 (half-n) and piece:1,-1,0 (half-n).

finish.summary: Built a small shelf unit: three full bases in a row with two-compartment bins as cubbies, two half-base drawers in front, joint bolts locking the joints. meshClash is clear and check_build has no errors. Caps on the open faces were not applied: capOpenFaces clashes with the drawer frames (5 mm into hex-drawer-frame-s) and skipping faces did not clear it, so 20 open faces remain (info only). The 50 kg book rating cannot be verified by the configurator and is not claimed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
